scope: Proposition 3.2 (Simultaneous inverse comparison) of the manuscript “Generalized ionization energies for full Coulomb atoms” (preprints/Generalized-ionization-energies-for-full-Coulomb-atoms-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 263 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1450c11be0743629), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a universal constant Ccap with the following property. Fix M ≥ 2, 0 < hl < hh < ∞, 0 < ξ < hl/16. 10 For all sufficiently far systems along Equation (2.1), at every j < J∗ there is an event Gj ∈ Fj such that, with r = rj, P(Gc j ) ≤ Cr25 . On Gj, the following assertions hold simultaneously for r ≤ dy ≤ 4Mr and hl ≤ h ≤ hh: d4 yH′ j(y) ≤ Ccap, d6 yµj(y) > kh3/2 =⇒ d4 yH′ j(y) ≥ h − ξ, d6 yµj(y) < kh3/2 =⇒ d4 yH′ j(y) ≤ h + ξ. (3.6) The probability constant and the threshold for sufficiently far systems may depend on the displayed fixed parameters and on the fixed packet conventions; Ccap is independent of the band and accuracy parameters.
